question: A flight is to be made along the parallel of latitude from A at 48°00’N 04°00’W to B at 48°00’N 02°27’E. Calculate the distance.
An aircraft flies for 1000 NM along a rhumb line track of 090°(T) from C at 36°00’N 174°45’E to D. What is the longitude of D?

The following rhumb line tracks and distances are flown; starting from E in latitude 50°N. E to F 000°(T) 300 NM, F to G 090°(T) 300 NM, G to H 180°(T) 300 NM. What is the rhumb line bearing and distance of H from E?
What is the track and distance measured along the parallel of latitude of 80°S from 176°15’W to 179°45’E?
In which latitude is a difference in longitude of 44°10’ the equivalent of a departure of 2295 NM?
An aircraft leaves J (36°00’S 130°14’E) at 0946 UTC, flying a rhumb line track of 270° at FL100, temperature 0°C, Mach 0.81, wind component 35 kt tail. What is the aircraft’s position at 1004 UTC?

At which latitude is the departure in NM between two points equal to:
 (i). their difference in longitude in minutes? 
(ii). half their difference in longitude in minutes?
At latitude 52°N, what is the departure between the meridians of 136°16’W and 43°44’E, and what is the shortest distance between the same points?

An aircraft leaves position L in latitude 37°S and makes good the following tracks and ground speeds: L to M 270°(T) 310 kt (80 mins), M to N 180°(T) 280 kt, N to P 090°(T) 250 kt (93.5 mins to P). P is due south of L. Calculate the distance and time from M to N.
Aircraft Q flies at GS 301 kt along 46°N for 10° of longitude. Aircraft R flies between the same meridians in the same time. What is the latitude of R’s track?

Aircraft S leaves 36°N 10°E at 1522, flies 090°(T) at 470 kt, turns at 13°E onto 180°(T) at 460 kt. Aircraft T leaves 30°N 10°E at 1522 and flies 090°(T) at 150 kt. 1) Which aircraft reaches 30°N 13°E first? 2) What time? 3) Where is the other aircraft?
An aircraft starts at 04°10’S 178°22’W and heads true north for 2950 NM, then turns 90° left and flies 314 km. What is its final position?
An aircraft at position 50°N 006°E travels 300 NM due South, then 300 NM due East, then 300 NM due North, then 300 NM due West. What is its final position relative to its start point?
An aircraft departs 04°00’N 170°00’W and flies 600 NM South, then East, then North, then West. What is its final position?
An aircraft is flying around Earth eastwards along 60°N at 240 kt. What ground speed must another aircraft have along the equator to complete a full circle in the same time?
Your position is 58°33’N 174°00’W. You fly exactly 6 NM eastwards. What is your new position?
